newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Losses to Slovak blue chips pull BSE lower.
newsitem.headline: Losses to Slovak blue chips pull BSE lower.

text.p: Leading Slovak shares closed mostly lower in flat trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Friday, pulling the SAX index down 0.59 points to 200.32.
Oil refinery Slovnaft, closed down 16 at 920 crowns, while the oil and gas storage firm Nafta did not trade on Friday.
Steel maker VSZ dominated the bourse's floor, with 2,161 shares traded, closing down 10 at 620 crowns.
Brokers said the general decline of the market should continue.
"Still there are some issues posting the gains, but on the bids of some 20-50 shares, which definitely cannot change the trend on the bourse," Patrik Granec of Slovenska Sporitelna said.
"Despite nice volumes, I don't see VSZ rising in the near future, as its accepted price has been hovering between 620 to 630 for a relatively long time," Granec added.
Overall volume increased to 381,788 shares, from 180,905 sharees traded on Thursday, while the turnover dipped to 152.17 million crowns, from 185.81 million.
